Thanks again for the time today — great conversation. Short recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

Summary of your perf targets (as I heard them):
- Time-to-first-token (TTFT): median <= 150 ms, p95 <= 350 ms
- Streaming: prefer WebSocket for lower latency; SSE acceptable as fallback
- Chunk cadence: client-visible partial chunks ~200–400 ms cadence (smooth UX for partial results)
- Concurrency / throughput: ~200 concurrent streaming sessions during peak, sustained token throughput ~100k tokens/minute (bursts higher)

Action items we committed to: 
1) Run an initial PoC with your sample traffic and our default streaming config (WebSocket). We'll provide a short benchmark report (TTFT, p50/p95, chunk cadence distribution).
2) Dev deep-dive to validate chunking cadence, WSS keepalive, and fallback to SSE.
3) Draft an SLO proposal showing recommended instance sizing / Dedicated capacity options and cost/latency trade-offs.

Can you confirm the sample prompt set and whether Michael (procurement) should be on the PoC timeline/contract conversations? I’ll kick off bench runs after you confirm the sample traffic and the preferred PoC week (we suggested May 24–28).

Thanks — Aditya

From: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: TTFT & Streaming SLOs — technical approach and preliminary bench

Thanks Sam — copying the technical plan and preliminary numbers here so everyone has visibility. High level PoC plan: 
1) Ingest your acme_sample_traffic.csv and generate a 2-hour replay match for peak and off-peak windows.
2) Run streaming bench against Redwood-hosted Dedicated capacity (GPU pool with low-latency networking) using WebSocket transport and our streaming chunking layer.
3) Measure TTFT (first token delivered from API) p50/p95, chunk cadence distribution (ms between client-visible chunks), sustained token throughput, and degradation curves vs concurrency.
4) Deliver: ttft_benchmark_results.csv (attached), 1-page SLO recommendation, and an ops-runbook for production rollout.

Preliminary numbers (local bench, representative model config):
- Model: redwood-13b-quant-v2 (inference-optimized)
- Instance: Dedicated A100-equivalent pool, small batching and KV cache warm
- Measured TTFT: median ~120 ms, p95 ~280 ms (WebSocket, single-request warm cache)
- Chunk cadence: median ~180 ms, 75th ~260 ms — most short prompts produce 1–3 small chunks quickly; longer responses stream continuous chunks at ~150–300 ms depending on tokenization
- Concurrency: stable at 200 concurrent streams in our test; performance shows graceful degradation up to ~320 concurrent streams where p95 TTFT rises to ~500 ms without additional pooling

Notes / tradeoffs:
- TTFT is most sensitive to cold KV cache and kernel selection; warm cache + tuned kernels reduces p95 significantly.
- Continuous batching improves throughput but increases single-request TTFT slightly; for strict TTFT targets we run small (per-connection) batching and rely on Dedicated capacity for headroom.
- WebSocket provides slightly better TTFT than SSE in our measurements (lower transport overhead and faster push), but SSE remains a solid fallback for environments where WSS is blocked.

Attachments: ttft_benchmark_results.csv (detailed run), slo_proposal.pdf (draft SLO and sizing)

Next asks from us:
- Confirm PoC week (May 24–28 works).
- Provide any additional edge-case prompts you want included (e.g., long context windows, multi-turn history).
- Confirm whether you want Redwood to run the PoC on a hosted Dedicated pool (recommended) or if you want to run in your cloud account (we can support both).

Happy to jump on a 30-minute tech call early next week to go through the bench config — propose Mon May 17 10:00am PT.

Thanks — Dev
Dev Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
